**Audience:** network, platform, database, identity, and security engineers.
**Prerequisite:** Module A0 (orientation) from the
[compliance track](compliance-track.html) — you need the FedRAMP 20x timeline
and the evidence-slot model in your head before you build, because every
build here ends by **landing evidence**, not just by working.
**Companion:** each module lists the matching external courses from the
[vendor training catalog](vendor-training-catalog.html).

## The rule of this track

> A module is done when the thing works **and** the conformance adapter can
> see it. Every lab ends with an evidence artifact in a place the
> [`fedramp_aan_catalog`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/tree/main/src/uiao/adapters/fedramp_aan_catalog)
> slot mappings can bind.

## Module B1 — Landing zone, IPAM & DDI (Book 01) {#module-b1-landing-zone-ipam-ddi-book-01}

- **Read:** Book 01 (SSA Landing Zone, IPAM & FedRAMP).
- **Build:** the DDI core — authoritative IPAM, DNS, DHCP, and PKI issuance
  for the landing zone. The reference stack is Infoblox; the UIAO
  modernization adapters for
  [BlueCat](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/tree/main/src/uiao/adapters) and
  Infoblox cover directory migration into it.
- **Lab:** stand up (or simulate with fixtures) an IPAM inventory export and
  bind it as slot-02 addressing evidence.
- **Vendor training:** Infoblox education, BlueCat learning, Microsoft
  AZ-700 (Azure networking for the landing-zone side) — see
  [catalog §Networking & DDI](vendor-training-catalog.html#networking-ddi).

## Module B2 — Network & telecommunications modernization (Books 02–03) {#module-b2-network-telecommunications-modernization-books-0203}

- **Read:** Book 02 (SD-WAN, SASE, unified communications — Teams Phone,
  Amazon Connect) and Book 03 (Entra ID, ZTNA, active governance).
- **Build:** application-aware transport — SD-WAN path policy keyed to
  application identity, SASE enforcement, ZTNA in front of legacy telecom
  patterns.
- **Lab:** author one application-aware path policy and one ZTNA access
  policy; export the policy state and bind it as slot-03 network evidence.
- **Vendor training:** Cisco U / Networking Academy (SD-WAN), Microsoft
  SC-300 (Entra), AWS Skill Builder (Amazon Connect), Fortinet / Palo Alto
  (SASE) — see [catalog §Networking & DDI](vendor-training-catalog.html#networking-ddi)
  and [§Identity & zero trust](vendor-training-catalog.html#identity-zero-trust).

## Module B3 — Data platform modernization (Books 04–06) {#module-b3-data-platform-modernization-books-0406}

- **Read:** Book 04 (SQL Server Authentication Modernization), Book 05
  (SQL Server Implementation Guide — the runbook), Book 06 (Database
  Consolidation & Network Physics).
- **Build:** Entra-integrated SQL Server authentication (no SQL logins),
  then the consolidation architecture Book 06 derives from network physics
  (latency budgets, placement, failure domains).
- **Lab:** execute the Book 05 runbook against a lab instance; capture the
  authentication-mode evidence and bind it as slot-01 identity evidence.
- **Vendor training:** Microsoft DP-300, SQL Server security learning paths
  — see [catalog §Data platform](vendor-training-catalog.html#data-platform).

## Module B4 — Privileged access (Book 07) {#module-b4-privileged-access-book-07}

- **Read:** Book 07 (Privileged Access Management — Entra PIM + PAW).
- **Build:** role-activation workflows in PIM (eligibility, activation,
  approval, review) and the privileged-access-workstation tier model.
- **Lab:** configure one eligible role with activation approval + access
  review; export the PIM audit trail and bind it as slot-01/slot-05
  evidence.
- **Vendor training:** Microsoft SC-300, AZ-500; SANS privileged-access
  coursework — see [catalog §Identity & zero trust](vendor-training-catalog.html#identity-zero-trust).

## Module B5 — Detect & protect (Books 08–10) {#module-b5-detect-protect-books-0810}

- **Read:** Book 08 (Vulnerability Management — Defender VM + KEV), Book 09
  (Data Protection — Purview + Key Vault CMK), Book 10 (SIEM / XDR
  Detection — Sentinel).
- **Build:** the telemetry spine — Defender VM assessment with KEV
  prioritization; Purview sensitivity labeling + customer-managed keys;
  Sentinel analytics rules, incidents, and automation.
- **Lab:** one end-to-end detection: seed a vulnerable/exposed condition,
  watch it surface in Defender VM, alert in Sentinel, and close with an
  evidence export bound to slot-04 telemetry (and slot-06 for the
  configuration-drift angle).
- **Vendor training:** Microsoft SC-200 (Sentinel/Defender), SC-401
  (Purview/information security), Splunk & Elastic for portable SIEM
  fundamentals — see [catalog §Security operations](vendor-training-catalog.html#security-operations).

## Module B6 — Resilience & governance (Books 11–14) {#module-b6-resilience-governance-books-1114}

- **Read:** Book 11 (Business Continuity), Book 12 (Supply Chain Risk
  Management), Book 13 (Program Management & Governance), Book 14 (PII
  Processing & Transparency).
- **Build:** the contingency architecture (alternate processing/storage,
  CP-4 test harness); the SBOM pipeline (Syft/Trivy-class generation,
  CycloneDX/SPDX VDR, VER submission flow for BOD 26-04); the PM governance
  charter artifacts; PII processing-transparency records.
- **Lab:** generate an SBOM for a real service, produce the VDR document,
  and bind it as slot-06 evidence; run one tabletop contingency test and
  bind the results as slot-07 continuity evidence.
- **Vendor training:** CISA Learning (incident/continuity), FedRAMP PMO
  materials (20x submission), OWASP/Linux Foundation SBOM resources — see
  [catalog §Federal & compliance](vendor-training-catalog.html#federal-compliance).

## Capstone — one module, evidence-complete

Pick one module (B1–B6). Implement or lab-simulate it end-to-end, land the
evidence where the slot mapping binds it, then regenerate the verdicts:

```bash
uiao ksi evaluate --ir ./output/ir/tenant.ir.json --out ./output/ksi/tenant.ksi.json
uiao oscal ksi-ar --output exports/oscal/ksi-ar.json
```

Completion means the Assessment Results show your module's slot verdict fed
by **your** artifact — the same bar as UIAO_125's Operator track ("clean
walker/drift run"), applied to the AAN vertical.

## Sequencing note

B1 → B2 → B3 is a real dependency chain (addressing before transport before
data placement). B4–B6 can run in parallel after B2. Track A modules can be
interleaved freely; many teams pair each B-module with its A-module
(B1↔A2, B2↔A1/A3, B3↔A1, B4↔A1/A5, B5↔A4/A6, B6↔A6/A7).
